answers.explanation: Then came Algol and PL/1, and now C and C++.
They came between assembly and C.
Usually a mix: assembly at the lowest levels, C for the main body, and C, C++, and scripting languages for system programs.
Boot code and register-level details need exact control of the CPU.
High-level languages make an OS easier to port.
That's the trade-off on the slides, though modern compilers shrink it.
Software imitates one kind of hardware on top of another.
Scripting languages are common for system programs.
